name: Titan
summary: Across the Great Dark Beyond, the titans travel from world to world, seeking places to shape and order. Long ago, they came to Azeroth, defeated the Old Gods, raised great works, and prepared the world for life before departing among the stars.

sections.title: Architects of the Cosmos
sections.body: Across the Great Dark Beyond, the titans journey as cosmic giants of primordial matter and arcane magic. They carry the forces of order and creation, seeking sleeping worlds to cultivate. There they raise continents, calm the elements, and shape life. Stone, iron, and sea constructs guard their works and keep the balance they sought.

sections.title: The Ordering of Azeroth
sections.body: When the Pantheon found Azeroth long ago, chaotic elemental lords and the horrific Old Gods held the world in their grip. The titans drove the elementals into pocket planes and sealed the Old Gods beneath the earth. They shaped great biomes and built vaults such as Uldaman. Then they entrusted five great dragons, the Dragon Aspects, with the land, magic, time, and life, and journeyed back among the stars.

sections.title: The Fallen Champion
sections.body: Sargeras once stood among the titans as their greatest warrior and defender. Yet the deep cosmic darkness and demonic malevolence he fought filled him with fear and despair. He rejected his kin's work and embraced nihilism. To extinguish all creation rather than let it fall to corruption, he founded the Burning Legion.

faq.q: Are the titans still alive and on Azeroth?
faq.answer: The titans departed Azeroth long ago for the Great Dark Beyond, after defeating the Old Gods and ordering the world. They left watchers, stone and iron constructs, and buried vaults to oversee their design.

faq.q: Why do the dwarves care so much about the titans?
faq.answer: Dwarves descend from the earthen, subterranean stone beings the titans fashioned to carve the world's foundations. Through archaeology and the excavation of ruins such as Bael Modan and Uldaman, dwarves seek their forgotten lineage.

The Pantheon is the titans' governing council, led by the Highfather Aman'Thul. Its members include Khaz'goroth the shaper of worlds, Eonar the life-binder, Norgannon the keeper of celestial magics, Golganneth the lord of skies, and Aggramar, who replaced Sargeras as champion.

faq.q: Did the titans create the Dragon Aspects?
faq.answer: Yes. Before leaving Azeroth, the Pantheon sent its power through the keepers to bless five proto-dragons. Alexstrasza, Ysera, Malygos, Nozdormu, and Neltharion received immense power to safeguard life, nature, magic, time, and the earth.

Sargeras was once the Pantheon's champion, defending the cosmos against chaos and demons. The darkness he witnessed drove him to despair and madness. He broke with his brethren to form the Burning Legion and burn down the ordered universe.

faq.q: Did a titan fall in Silithus?
faq.answer: The Qiraji Prophet Skeram recorded prophecies claiming that a titan battled an ancient evil in Silithus's southern deserts and fell. Scholars and explorers still debate whether the fallen being was a true titan or one of their constructs.

angles.text: As a dwarf, you revere the titans as the divine Makers. The Explorers' League and King Magni Bronzebeard seek your origins among titanic relics.
As a gnome, you share a mechanical legacy from titanic creations. That legacy drives your affinity for clockwork design and excavation.
As a mage, you wield arcane magic, the titans' fundamental lifeblood. Its ordered principles trace to enchantments the Pantheon wove across the world.
As a miner, you dig deep into the earth and may uncover pristine titan-forged metal and foundations older than recorded history.
